title: Regional power-amortized token economics (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad to explore how regional power prices and amortized GPU purchase/commit costs change per-token COGS for Hosted API across batch sizes and cache hit rates. This is intentionally informal — loose equations, sample numbers, and recommendations for the Optimize roadmap.

High-level approach (inputs we vary):
- region_power ($/kWh)
- gpu_hour_price ($/GPU-hour equivalent: includes amortized reserved + maintenance + networking)
- amort_window_months (how we amortize committed GPUs)
- avg_tokens_per_req (user-level tokens/request)
- avg_generated_tokens (model outputs)
- batch_size (effective continuous batching window)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (fraction of reqs served from KV/prefix cache)
- model_family (gptx-13b, gptx-70b, etc.)

Assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline model: gptx-13b running on A100-like hardware equivalent. Baseline gpu_hour_price = $4.50 (amortized reserved + ops).
- Power draw average: 400W active per GPU. So kWh per hour = 0.4 kWh.
- region_power baseline (US-west): $0.12/kWh. Power cost per GPU-hour = 0.4 * 0.12 = $0.048. Add 5% facility overhead -> $0.0504.
- Combined baseline gpu_hour_price_including_power = 4.50 + 0.05 = $4.55.
- Avg tokens per request = 60 prompt tokens, avg generated = 70 tokens -> 130 tokens total.
- Requests per second (RPS) per GPU depends on model and batch sizing; use throughput table below.

Rough throughput vs batch size (gptx-13b, short seq):
- batch=1 -> 30 tokens/sec per GPU
- batch=4 -> 110 tokens/sec per GPU
- batch=8 -> 200 tokens/sec per GPU
- batch=16 -> 330 tokens/sec per GPU
(These are synthetic throughput numbers for sensitivity; real numbers should come from serving-runtime benchmarks.)

Per-token cost formula (simplified):
- cost_per_gpu_hour = gpu_hour_price_including_power
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600
- raw_token_cogs = cost_per_gpu_hour / tokens_per_gpu_hour
- effective_token_cogs = raw_token_cogs * (1 - kv_cache_hit_rate) + kv_cache_marginal_cost (small)

Sample calculations (baseline region)
1) batch=1, throughput=30 t/s -> tokens/hour = 108k -> raw_token_cogs = 4.55 / 108000 = $0.0000421 per token -> ~0.00421 cents/token
2) batch=8, throughput=200 t/s -> tokens/hour = 720k -> raw_token_cogs = 4.55 / 720000 = $0.00000632 per token -> ~0.000632 cents/token

Impact of kv cache: assume kv_cache_hit_rate = 0.35 and kv_cache_marginal_cost accounted as $0.0000005/token for hits (network + read). Then effective_token_cogs for batch=8:
- raw = 0.00000632
- effective = raw * (1 - 0.35) + 0.0000005 * 0.35 = 0.00000411 + 0.000000175 = 0.000004285 -> ~0.0004285 cents/token

Regional sensitivity example (batch=8, amort_window=36 months):
Region A (US-west): region_power=0.12/kWh -> power per GPU-hour = $0.0504 (as above) -> included in 4.55 -> token COGS ~0.00000632 raw
Region B (Nordic): region_power=0.06/kWh -> power per GPU-hour = 0.024 -> facility overhead 5% -> 0.0252 -> combined gpu_hour = 4.5252 -> raw_token_cogs = 4.5252 / 720000 = 0.00000628 (tiny change)
Region C (Japan): region_power=0.25/kWh -> power per GPU-hour = 0.1 -> after overhead 0.105 -> combined = 4.605 -> raw_token_cogs = 4.605 / 720000 = 0.0000064
Observation: for large reserved amortized costs, delta due to regional power is small vs amortized GPU price. Power matters more when GPU amortization shrinks (e.g., burst or on-demand pricing) or when GPUs are high-power devices.

Amortization/window sensitivity (example batch=8, region US-west):
- amort_window=12 months -> gpu_hour_price increases to reflect faster amortization: assume $6.00 -> combined 6.05 -> raw_token_cogs = 6.05 / 720000 = 0.00000840
- amort_window=60 months -> gpu_hour_price $3.25 -> combined 3.30 -> raw_token_cogs = 3.30 / 720000 = 0.00000458
=> Changing amort window from 12->60 months moved token COGS by ~0.00000382 -> ~ nearly 60% of the baseline token COGS delta. This is larger than region power variation.

Edge case: short-sequence, high-QPS workloads where batching is limited by latency SLOs:
- If batch_size forced to 1 or 2 due to P95 latency targets, token COGS jumps 6x-10x vs optimistic batching. That is the primary leaver on per-token cost for many interactive workloads.

Table: illustrative per-token COGS (raw) under different regions, batch sizes (numbers in USD per token)
Region | batch=1 | batch=4 | batch=8 | batch=16
US-west | 0.0000421 | 0.0000115 | 0.00000632 | 0.00000423
Nordic | 0.0000419 | 0.0000114 | 0.00000628 | 0.00000420
Japan | 0.0000425 | 0.0000116 | 0.00000640 | 0.00000427

Notes (what this means for product decisions):
- Focus 1: For hosted API margin improvements, the biggest lever is increasing effective batching and/or accepting slightly higher P95 for small percent of traffic (can be handled with tiered latency policies).
- Focus 2: Cache hit rate improvements (prefix caching, smart routing to cached model variants) compound with batching. Example: 35% cache hit + batch 8 reduces effective token cogs materially vs batch=1 no cache.
- Focus 3: Regional power arbitrage is real but modest at our current reserved-cap-heavy cost structure. Regional focus is higher ROI when combined with: (a) lower reserved cost (e.g., spot) or (b) specialized high-power GPUs (H100 class) where power delta is bigger.

Operational recommendations (short list):
1) Product: implement latency-tiered routing demo for a mid-size customer to show 10-30% token cost reduction while keeping 99th latency SLA. (Owner: Tom)
2) Engineering: add a microbenchmark that outputs tokens/sec vs batch for top 4 model families under 3 seq-length profiles. Use that to build a throughput lookup table used by the Cost API. (Owner: Marta)
3) Optimize: prototype a region-aware placement rule that includes power and amortized reserved cost as inputs to the routing policy. Start with Nordic vs Japan vs US-west. (Owner: Liam)
4) Finance/Rev Ops: provide amortization curves for reserved commitments (12/36/60 months) across our major commitment classes so product can model scenarios dynamically.

Open questions / TODOs:
- We need real throughput numbers from serving-runtime on our model variants; the synthetic table above is only for sensitivity. (JIRA: JIRA-INF-2102)
- How do E2E networking costs (e.g., cross-region egress) change the benefit of shifting workload regionally? Add egress into region model.
- For KV cache cost: quantify real network/memstore read cost per hit (observability team to run measurement).

Quick decision heuristics (for Strategy):
- If > 40% of requests are low-seq and can tolerate 50-100ms extra latency, invest in batching-first routing and expect 30-60% reduction in per-token hardware COGS.
- If average request length > 400 tokens, power and model family start to matter more; prioritize model-family-specific placement.

References / links:
- CONFLUENCE-12345 (token economics primer)
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987 (placement rule prototype)

Last quick thought: this doc should seed a small spreadsheet that enumerates combinations of (region x amort-window x batch x kv-hit x model) and produces per-token cogs + margin vs list price. Next step: build that sheet and attach to the cost API used by pricing UI.

-- Aisha (notes, rough)
